item.description:
## A crashed script no longer gets stuck
A script that crashed right after starting could get stuck as "stopping" forever: `grove_status` showed it that way with no way out, `grove_stop_script` did nothing, and `grove_start_script` claimed it was already ready. Grove now reaps the process and reports its real exit code no matter when the crash happens.
## Warnings before you lose running scripts
- Quitting Grove with scripts still running now asks first, instead of stopping them silently. - Disconnecting a project with scripts running in it now says how many will be stopped.

## One project at a time
The sidebar now shows a single project. Switch projects from the menu at the top of the sidebar, or press ⌘1 to ⌘9.
- Search still covers every project, with results grouped by project. - Projects out of view that have something running or crashed stay listed at the bottom of the sidebar, one click away. - Grove remembers which project you were looking at. - Selecting a script from the menu bar switches the sidebar to its project.
## Fixes for macOS 27
- Opening a second pane no longer makes the window wider than your screen. Four panes fit in a normal window again, and you can drag the dividers to resize panes. Double-click a divider to even them out. - In a narrow pane, the toolbar hides the usage readout and status text instead of cutting off buttons. - App icons are back in the Open In menu.
